domain: sets of 25 distinct classes (a mod m), m | L=16, m >= 2, 0 <= a < m, pairwise disjoint with pairwise gcd <= 24; primes P=(2,)
domain_proof: Lemma A (result.md): any counterexample of size 25 reduces to one with every modulus dividing L_all = 16*9*5*7*11*13*17*19*23 with the same pairwise gcds; this branch covers exactly those reduced counterexamples whose moduli use only primes in P.

rules.statement: Canonical order: classes sorted by (m, a); only increasing index sequences enumerated.
rules.proof: Disjointness and the gcd condition are symmetric; equal classes are never disjoint (gcd(m,m)=m | 0), so each family is a set and has exactly one increasing listing.

rules.statement: Translation: the first (smallest in (m,a) order) class has a = 0.
rules.proof: Shifting all residues by -a_1 preserves every difference a_i - a_j, so disjointness and gcds are kept; the smallest class (m1,a1) becomes (m1,0), still smallest among classes of modulus m1 since 0 is the least residue, and classes of larger modulus stay larger. So every family has a translate with a_1 = 0.

rules.statement: Compatibility: a class is added only if it is disjoint from, and has gcd <= 24 with, every chosen class.
rules.proof: Both conditions are pairwise and required of every pair in a counterexample.

rules.statement: Colouring bound: if |chosen| + (number of colours in a greedy proper colouring of the candidate compatibility graph) < 25, prune.
rules.proof: Candidates are the classes compatible with all chosen ones and later in order. Any extension adds a clique of the compatibility graph on candidates; a clique meets each colour class (an independent set) at most once.

rules.statement: Multiplier: the second class (m2, a2) of the family (second in (m, a) order) has a2 = 0 or a2 | m2.
rules.proof: The affine maps x -> u x + t (u a unit mod L_P) send classes (m, a) to (m, (u a + t) mod m), keep every modulus, and keep disjointness and gcds, because g | (a_i - a_j) iff g | u (a_i - a_j) for gcd(u, g) = 1. Take the image of a family whose sorted list is lexicographically least. Its first class has a1 = 0 (else translate by -a1: moduli are fixed, so the first class becomes (m1, 0), smaller). Let (m2, a2) be its second class and d = gcd(a2, m2). Units mod L_P surject onto units mod m2, so some unit u has u a2 = d mod m2; x -> u x fixes (m1, 0), which stays first (moduli fixed, 0 least residue), and sends (m2, a2) to (m2, d). Every other class has modulus >= m2, so the new second class is <= (m2, d). If d < a2 this image is smaller, contradiction; hence a2 = d, i.e. a2 | m2 (a2 = 0 is allowed). R2 is the first half of this argument.
